newsitem.title: Russia: Russia's 1996 grain imports nearly doubled on 1995 levels. [CORRECTED 18:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia's 1996 grain imports nearly doubled on 1995 levels. [CORRECTED 18:42 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects throughout. Interfax new agency said it had erroneously reported 1995 import and export comparison figures, both in tonnage and dollar value terms.)

Russia's grain and flour imports of 5.1 million tonnes in 1996 were nearly double 1995's 2.7 million tonnes, representing a rise of 89 percent year-on-year, State Customs Committee figures showed on Tuesday.
The data, carried by Interfax news agency, put the value of last year's total grain and flour imports at $913.2 million against $395.4 million in 1995.
It said wheat and wheat-rye blend imports in 1996 of 2.7 million tonnes were 1.2 million tonnes higher than in 1995.
Wheat flour 1996 imports of 687,400 tonnes were 157,000 tonnes higher than in 1995.
Rye imports of 264,500 tonnes were 220,000 tonnes higher.
Barley imports of 1.4 million tonnes in 1996 were 789,000 tonnes higher than in 1995.
Exports of Russian grain and flour in 1996 of 642,800 tonnes slumped from 2.3 million tonnes in 1995.
Earnings from grain exports last year were $135.1 million against $192.2 million in 1995.
Wheat and wheat-rye blend exports of 343,000 tonnes in 1996 were 161,000 tonnes higher than in 1995, while rye exports of 8,800 tonnes were 345,000 tonnes less than in 1995.
Barley exports of 187,900 tonnes were 1.5 million tonnes less than in 1995, while wheat-flour exports of 103,000 tonnes were 5,000 tonnes higher than in 1995.
State Customs Committee figures do not include unregistered transactions.
